findings.affected_section: 07_FULL_PLAN.md §1 items 1 and 10; §12 D1 lines 373-379; §12 D2 line 407; §13 lines 526-552; §16 lines 620-636; §17 Docker evidence
findings.claim: The plan does not fail closed by binding every Docker mutation to the intended local Docker Desktop endpoint. A stale Docker context or DOCKER_HOST/DOCKER_CONTEXT override can redirect start, backup, restore, Compose, or cleanup operations to another daemon, including an external daemon expressly outside scope.
findings.evidence: D1 checks for Docker Desktop/Engine/CLI and conflicting daemons, and D2 says to recheck Docker context after reboot. Section 17 asks for context evidence. However, the CLI contract in §13 contains no mandatory endpoint/context assertion before each mutating command, §16 has no stop condition for a non-local context or environment override, and the plan simultaneously requires that the production VPS remain untouched in §1 and §18. Bundle 03_LOCAL_INFRASTRUCTURE_KNOWN.json states Docker runtime availability was false at the last gate, so no safe local endpoint identity is currently established.
findings.impact: A valid command intended for the laboratory can perform unauthorized external actions against an unrelated or production Docker daemon. Depending on the invoked operation, this can start workloads, expose secrets, overwrite state, or delete resources outside the approved Windows host.
findings.required_resolution: Make endpoint identity a mandatory invariant of every lab command. Record an approved local Docker Desktop context and endpoint class during post-install qualification; reject DOCKER_HOST, DOCKER_CONTEXT, TLS/SSH/TCP endpoints, unknown contexts, and daemon identity drift. Invoke Docker and Compose with an explicit approved context without changing the user's global context. Before every mutation, assert the local endpoint, Server OS=linux, expected Desktop daemon identity, and approved Compose project name; add non-local context or override presence to automatic stop conditions.
findings.acceptance_test: Create harmless sentinel contexts and environment overrides representing a non-local or unknown endpoint. For lab start, stop, backup, restore-drill, image operations, and cleanup paths, prove that each exits nonzero before its first mutating Docker API request and reports a redacted context mismatch. Prove the same commands proceed only with the preflight-recorded local Desktop endpoint, and that changing the global current context between commands cannot redirect them.

findings.affected_section: 07_FULL_PLAN.md §4.2; §12 D1 lines 368-381; §16 line 625; §21 lines 707-712; 03_LOCAL_INFRASTRUCTURE_KNOWN.json unknown_until_preflight; 08_PRIMARY_SOURCES.md Docker/Microsoft and Source acceptance rule
findings.claim: The Windows support preflight is a list of topics, not an executable support predicate. The plan cannot reproducibly decide supported versus unsupported Windows before download.
findings.evidence: D1 says to check edition/build/architecture, virtualization, WSL features, resources, App Control, users, and licensing, then stop on an unsupported Windows state. It defines no required fields, authoritative requirement snapshot, comparisons, PASS/BLOCKED rules, or treatment of an unknown value. Section 21 leaves the exact OS state open. Bundle 03 marks every relevant prerequisite unknown, while 08_PRIMARY_SOURCES.md requires current official platform requirements to be verified at execution time.
findings.impact: Two operators can classify the same host differently, or installation can begin with an unsupported or insufficiently evidenced host. The no-change preflight evidence would not prove that the installation prerequisites were actually satisfied.
findings.required_resolution: Define a versioned, machine-readable Windows eligibility record and decision table. It must bind redacted OS edition/build/architecture and servicing state, CPU architecture, hardware and firmware virtualization state, required optional-feature state, WSL state, resource thresholds, device-management policy, and license disposition to a dated authoritative Docker/Microsoft requirements snapshot. Unknown, unreadable, conflicting, or below-threshold fields must produce BLOCKED before download.
findings.acceptance_test: Run the preflight against fixtures covering supported, unsupported, below-threshold, unreadable, and contradictory states. Only the fully supported fixture may pass; all others must stop before network or installer activity. Evidence must include the rule-set version, authoritative source identifiers/timestamps, collected values, evaluated predicates, and a no-change attestation.

findings.claim: The WSL/Virtual Machine Platform transition is not specified as an auditable change transaction, and the touchset unjustifiably assumes one reboot.
findings.evidence: D2 requires an exact feature change set only if features are needed, followed by a post-reboot check. It does not define the before-state schema, WSL component/version/update state, pending-reboot state, exact commands or installer switches, update artifact provenance, elevation boundary, intermediate stop points, or resume procedure. Section 14 nevertheless declares 'one reboot'. Manual gates mention feature changes/reboot and Admin/UAC but do not bind approval to exact command bytes or post-reboot continuation.
findings.impact: Execution can silently expand from installation into feature enablement or WSL updating, require additional restarts, leave Windows in a partially changed state, or continue after reboot without evidence that the approved transaction is still the one being executed.
findings.required_resolution: Replace the single step with an explicit state machine: capture immutable before-state; derive an exact proposed delta; separately authorize every feature/package/update and elevation action; record official provenance; detect pending reboot; never promise a fixed reboot count; stop before each reboot; and resume only from a plan-hash-bound checkpoint after revalidating OS, WSL, features, update status, user identity, and Docker endpoint. If policy, Store/update availability, firmware, or an extra unapproved change is required, return BLOCKED-MANUAL.
findings.acceptance_test: Exercise table-driven cases for features already enabled, features disabled, WSL absent or unreadable, an update required, a pending reboot, policy-blocked updating, and a post-reboot state mismatch. Each case must yield the documented no-change/PASS/BLOCKED result. No feature, update, reboot, or resumed mutation may occur without an approval record containing the exact delta and frozen plan hash.

findings.affected_section: 07_FULL_PLAN.md §8.2 lines 251-256; §12 D1 line 376; §14 lines 580-588; §16 line 613; §17 Windows/Secrets/Operability evidence
findings.claim: The plan conflates the daily Windows owner, the identity supplying UAC credentials, Docker Desktop's control-plane users, and the owners of per-user configuration and data.
findings.evidence: Section 8 defines the secret root as accessible to the current Windows user and SYSTEM and trusts the Docker Desktop administrator/current user boundary. D1 only checks current groups and whether Admin/UAC is needed. No section identifies which account launches Desktop after reboot, owns Docker configuration and the lab root, receives control-plane access, or supplies over-the-shoulder elevation. Section 14 explicitly includes user Docker config and a user-only data root but provides no cross-account rule.
findings.impact: Installation performed with another administrator identity can create configuration or state under the wrong profile, deny the intended owner access, grant unintended local users Docker-equivalent control, or strand secrets and data after reboot/logoff.
findings.required_resolution: Define separate roles for intended daily owner, elevation credential, service/system components, and authorized Docker control-plane users. Resolve exact identities locally while storing only redacted identifiers in evidence. Run only the narrowly elevated installer action under UAC; do not run the full orchestration elevated. Specify ownership, group membership, ACL inheritance, required sign-out/restart, first launch, and per-user config/data locations. Stop if the intended ownership model cannot be achieved without broader access.
findings.acceptance_test: After installation and reboot, the intended non-elevated owner must reach only the approved local daemon and lab paths; secrets and user-only data must be inaccessible to a non-authorized local user; no lab configuration or data may be created under the elevation account's profile; and all group/ACL changes must match the approved before/after diff.

findings.affected_section: 07_FULL_PLAN.md §4.2 line 123; §12 D1 lines 373 and 379-381; §12 D2; §14 lines 580-588; §21 line 710; 03_LOCAL_INFRASTRUCTURE_KNOWN.json
findings.claim: Existing Docker Desktop detection and branching are incomplete. The plan checks only for unexpected docker-desktop data, then proceeds with a fresh-install-shaped D2 without defining safe behavior for a known prior installation.
findings.evidence: Bundle 03 marks existing Docker Desktop installation/data unknown. D1 mentions installed Desktop/Engine/CLI, conflicting daemons, and unexpected docker-desktop data. It does not require a complete inventory of installed packages, services, scheduled/startup components, user configs, contexts, managed WSL state, data-location settings, versions/channels, or ownership. There is no fresh-install versus repair/upgrade/downgrade decision branch.
findings.impact: A recognized but incompletely inventoried installation can be overwritten or migrated, existing images/volumes/settings can become inaccessible, and another user's Docker environment can be modified despite the stated stop condition.
findings.required_resolution: Define a non-mutating discovery inventory covering installed application records, executable provenance/version, services/startup entries, Docker contexts and environment overrides, WSL distributions/state, configured data locations, settings/policies, and ownership. Add mutually exclusive fresh-install, approved-upgrade, and BLOCKED-existing-state branches. Default to BLOCKED when any ownership, data, version, or migration fact is unresolved.
findings.acceptance_test: Test discovery against clean-host, partial-install, stopped-old-install, known-owned-data, unknown-owned-data, alternate-data-location, and conflicting-engine fixtures. Only a truly clean host or an explicitly approved and backed-up upgrade path may reach D2; all ambiguous states must stop without launching or repairing Docker.

findings.claim: The rollback table incorrectly labels uninstalling Docker Desktop 'before data' as non-destructive even though installation itself creates or changes managed WSL/data, network, application, and per-user state.
findings.evidence: Section 10 identifies the managed Linux data disk as persistent. Section 14 lists application files, managed WSL backend/data disk, virtual network, and user Docker config as the Windows touchset. Yet §15 offers ordinary stop/uninstall as the non-destructive rollback for 'Install before data' and supplies no exact-version uninstall semantics, state export, settings preservation, or before/after reconciliation. The recovery section merely forbids automatic reset or unregister.
findings.impact: Rollback can remove, orphan, migrate, or leave behind state and cannot prove restoration of the pre-install machine. On a host with prior components, ordinary uninstall can also affect data outside the new laboratory.
findings.required_resolution: Rename and split application rollback, feature rollback, and data recovery. Before installation, capture the exact approved baseline and vendor-documented install/uninstall effects for the selected version. Permit the fresh-install branch only after proving no pre-existing owned data is at risk; otherwise require an owner-approved backup/migration plan. Define what remains intentionally, what can be reverted safely, and what makes rollback BLOCKED. Never describe uninstall as non-destructive without a verified post-uninstall diff.
findings.acceptance_test: In a disposable Windows test environment using the exact installer, capture before-state, install, first-launch state, controlled stop/uninstall, and after-state. Account for every changed path, service, feature, WSL object, config, context, network, and startup entry. Pre-existing sentinel WSL/config/data objects must remain byte-identical, or the plan must classify the rollback as destructive and require a separate gate.

findings.claim: The proposed disk thresholds are internally insufficient and have no enforceable safety margin.
findings.evidence: Section 11 permits installation with 25 GiB free while allowing 20 GiB persistent Docker laboratory storage plus 5 GiB backups. That consumes the entire stated minimum before accounting for Docker Desktop application/managed-disk overhead, image pull or build transients, logs, encryption temporaries, PostgreSQL dump staging, isolated restore volumes, or a Windows free-space reserve. The limits are described as soft caps or proposals, and no enforcement/monitoring mechanism is specified.
findings.impact: Image pulls, backup encryption, VHDX growth, or a restore drill can exhaust the host volume, destabilize Windows/Docker Desktop, corrupt writes, or make recovery impossible precisely when extra space is needed.
findings.required_resolution: Replace the thresholds with a budget equation covering existing Docker state, application and managed-disk overhead, steady-state images/volumes/cache, worst-case pull/build temporary space, backup staging plus encrypted output, isolated restore duplication, logs, and a non-consumable host reserve. Select exact volumes/data roots during preflight, enforce hard high-water marks before every growth operation, and define alert, stop, cleanup-approval, and VHDX growth/reclamation procedures.
findings.acceptance_test: For start, pull/build, backup, and restore-drill, inject free-space and projected-growth values immediately below and above each threshold. Below-threshold cases must stop before writes; allowed cases must preserve the declared host reserve at peak measured usage. Evidence must show resolved volume, current free space, projected peak, cap, reserve, and result.

findings.claim: The plan does not qualify the actual Windows storage locations and protection properties for Docker-managed sensitive data, the user-only root, or backup staging.
findings.evidence: The architecture places PostgreSQL/n8n data in named volumes on Docker Desktop's managed Linux disk and secrets/evidence/backups in a Windows user-only root. Only the secret-root ACL is described. D1 checks free disk but not resolved data paths, drive type, reparse/synchronization behavior, ACLs of all roots, host at-rest protection, or whether temporary plaintext backup material can land elsewhere. Section 21 leaves backup destination and key custody open.
findings.impact: Sensitive database or workflow data can be placed on a shared, synchronized, removable, unexpectedly redirected, or insufficiently protected location. Backup staging can leave plaintext remnants outside the intended ACL boundary, and a data-root move can become an unreviewed migration.
findings.required_resolution: Before installation, resolve and approve every application, managed-data, secret, evidence, backup, and temporary-staging root. Verify ownership/ACLs, reparse points, synchronization status, drive type, filesystem capability, free-space policy, and applicable at-rest protection. Explicitly reject Vault/repository/cloud-sync/shared/removable/network locations unless separately approved. Define an encrypted no-plaintext-staging backup flow and treat later data-root relocation as a destructive migration gate.
findings.acceptance_test: Preflight must fail closed for a broad-ACL root, redirected/reparse root, synchronized folder, disallowed drive type, unresolved managed-data location, or unprotected location contrary to the approved data classification. A valid run must record redacted canonical paths, volume identities, ACL summaries, protection state, and prove that backup creation leaves no plaintext artifact outside the approved staging boundary.

findings.claim: Exact-version installation is specified, but persistent version drift and Docker Desktop update change control are not.
findings.evidence: D2 locks an installer version/build/channel and D9 binds results to Desktop/Engine versions. The owner runbook is expected to include update, but no update policy, settings baseline, drift gate, compatibility rerun, backup requirement, downgrade feasibility, or rollback procedure appears in the plan. The CLI contract does not require start/verify to stop when Desktop, Engine, Compose, WSL, or settings differ from the qualified inventory.
findings.impact: A later runtime or settings change can invalidate containment, networking, mount behavior, evidence, and compatibility while the persistent laboratory still appears approved.
findings.required_resolution: Define the permitted update setting and drift policy for the selected channel. Persist the qualified Desktop/Engine/Compose/WSL/settings inventory; make lab start and verification fail closed on unapproved drift. Add a controlled update workflow requiring current official acquisition evidence, backup/restore readiness, capability and exposure regression tests, owner approval, and an explicit rollback or BLOCKED outcome.
findings.acceptance_test: Alter each recorded version/settings field in a fixture or disposable installation. Normal lab start must stop before workload mutation. The update workflow may clear the stop only after acquisition validation, backup, restart, complete required regression matrix, and a new approved inventory; failed qualification must leave the prior data recoverable.

findings.affected_section: 07_FULL_PLAN.md §4.2 line 123; §11 line 343; §12 D1 line 375; §16 lines 608-625; 03_LOCAL_INFRASTRUCTURE_KNOWN.json App Control/antivirus unknown
findings.claim: App Control and antivirus are merely inventoried; the plan has no fail-closed policy for unreadable policy, quarantine, runtime blocking, or requests for exclusions.
findings.evidence: D1 says to check App Control/antivirus, while §11 prohibits automatic security-tool changes. Neither D1 nor the stop conditions define what evidence is sufficient, how to distinguish policy enforcement from ordinary failure, whether retries are allowed after quarantine, or whether an operator may create an exclusion. Bundle 03 explicitly says these restrictions are unknown.
findings.impact: The installation can fail partially or produce misleading hash/runtime results, and an operator may weaken endpoint protection ad hoc to make Docker work.
findings.required_resolution: Define acceptable policy evidence and explicit UNKNOWN/BLOCKED outcomes. Never disable protection or add exclusions as automatic remediation. Capture only redacted relevant block/quarantine events; stop after a policy-caused failure; require separately documented organizational authorization for any exception; then rerun acquisition and integrity checks from clean official bytes.
findings.acceptance_test: Simulate unreadable policy, installer quarantine, executable runtime block, and an exclusion request. Every case must stop without changing security controls or repeatedly launching the blocked file. A permitted case must show no protection change and produce the expected policy/no-block evidence.

findings.claim: UAC and reboot gates lack operator-safety controls at the moment of disruption.
findings.evidence: The plan requires approval for Admin/UAC and exact feature changes/reboot but does not require an immediate pre-reboot confirmation, unsaved-work acknowledgement, AC-power/readiness check, no-auto-reboot installer mode, restart deadline, post-reboot owner presence, or prevention of automatic continuation. Section 14 assumes one reboot without a documented resume token.
findings.impact: An unattended or unexpected restart can interrupt unrelated user work, and post-reboot automation can continue under changed state or identity without renewed validation.
findings.required_resolution: Make elevation and reboot interactive stop points. Show exact command, affected components, expected interruption, and rollback limits immediately before UAC. Prohibit automatic reboot. Require explicit owner confirmation after saving work, write a non-secret plan-hash-bound resume checkpoint, and after reboot rerun identity, OS/feature, WSL, policy, Docker endpoint, and pending-reboot checks before requesting authorization to continue.
findings.acceptance_test: Force installer outcomes of no-reboot, reboot-required, cancelled UAC, and unexpected pending reboot. The process must never restart Windows itself, must never auto-resume a mutation after boot, and must reject a stale checkpoint, changed plan hash, changed user, or changed prerequisite state.

findings.claim: Port 5678 is checked only during preflight, with no immediate pre-bind revalidation or explicit occupied-port outcome.
findings.evidence: D1 checks availability of loopback port 5678. Section 16 stops when a bind is not loopback-only but does not define a stop for a later port collision. The CLI contract requires idempotent start but does not state how it reports another process already owning the port.
findings.impact: State can change between preflight and start, causing confusing failures or tempting an operator to choose an unreviewed port or broader bind.
findings.required_resolution: Revalidate IPv4 and IPv6 ownership immediately before start, distinguish this lab's existing listener from an unrelated process, and return a specific BLOCKED-PORT result. Do not auto-select another port or broaden the bind; any port change must be an explicit reviewed configuration change.
findings.acceptance_test: Bind 5678 with an unrelated local sentinel after preflight and run lab start. It must exit nonzero without starting the project or selecting another port. With the already-running approved lab listener, idempotent start must identify it correctly and preserve loopback-only exposure.
